description: Routes one signal to either of two outputs, choosing between them by comparing a second voltage against a split point

params.text: In the UNI position the split point is read as 0V to 10V, and in the BI position 5V is taken off it so it runs -5V to 5V
Sets the voltage the modulator is compared against, 0 to 10 before the polarity switch shifts it
Adds a fixed offset of -10V to 10V to whatever leaves the LOW output, despite the panel and the maker's manual calling it an attenuator
Adds a fixed offset of -10V to 10V to whatever leaves the HIGH output, despite the panel and the maker's manual calling it an attenuator

inputs.text: The signal routed to one output or the other; with nothing patched here the modulator voltage is routed instead
The voltage compared against the split point to choose which output is used; with nothing patched here both outputs stay at 0V
Shifts the split point, 10V adding the whole 0 to 10 span to the SPLIT knob and -10V taking it away
Shifts the LOW offset, 10V adding the whole -10V to 10V span to the LOW ATT knob and -10V taking it away
Shifts the HIGH offset, 10V adding the whole -10V to 10V span to the HIGH ATT knob and -10V taking it away

outputs.text: Carries the signal while the modulator voltage is below the split point, with the LOW ATT offset added, and 0V at every other moment
Carries the signal while the modulator voltage is at or above the split point, with the HIGH ATT offset added, and 0V at every other moment

notes: Both outputs hold 0V until a voltage reaches MOD; without it nothing is routed, whatever is patched into AUD.
